claims.claim: The energy in the sunlight on your skin spent more than a hundred thousand years getting out of the Sun.
claims.source_checked: https://solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml (read, Last Updated January 14, 2025); api.crossref.org/works/10.1086/172103 and /10.1023/A:1022952621810 (metadata only, no abstract); ADS (ui.adsabs.harvard.edu, articles.adsabs.harvard.edu, doi.org->adsabs.harvard.edu) and link.springer.com unreachable (DNS fail / proxy 403); Firecrawl out of credits
claims.note: The wording is true per an A2 source I did read: NASA MSFC says the core's energy is carried by photons through the radiative zone and 'an individual photon takes about a million years to finally reach the interface layer', so >1e5 years holds. But SOURCES entry 2 is not acceptable as written: (a) its cited figures (Mitalas & Sills 1.7e5 yr and the 0.090 cm step; Stix Kelvin-Helmholtz ~3e7 yr) could not be opened in this pass, only their Crossref metadata (titles, ApJ 401, 759, 1992; Sol. Phys. 212, 3-6, 2003) matches; (b) it says the Stix abstract was 'read at the publisher by the 2026-11-17 fact-check'. This 2026-11-17 pass could not reach the publisher, so SOURCES must not claim that. Cite who actually read it, or drop the claim; (c) A3: NASA MSFC, already cited in entries 4 and 6, gives ~1e6 years, a figure that differs from Mitalas & Sills' 1.7e5, and entry 2 does not record it. Change: add MSFC's 'about a million years' to entry 2 as an A2 source for the hook, record the disagreement with Mitalas & Sills, and fix the Stix provenance line. Also have Mitalas & Sills and Stix read where ADS/Springer are reachable, or rest the hook on MSFC alone. No change to the spoken line is needed.

claims.claim: A4: a viewer who swipes after the first sentence leaves believing the energy reaching their skin took over 100,000 years to leave the Sun (and is not told the light itself is that old).
claims.note: The first sentence is about the energy, not the light. It does not repeat the popular false form ('this sunlight is 100,000 years old'). Its content is true per MSFC (~1e6 yr radiative crossing, see claim 1). Nothing false is left at second two.

claims.claim: The trip from the Sun to you took eight minutes.
claims.source_checked: https://physics.nist.gov/cgi-bin/cuu/Value?c (c = 299 792 458 m/s, exact); https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/earthfact.html (semimajor axis 149.598e6 km, perihelion 147.095e6 km, aphelion 152.100e6 km). IAU 2012 Resolution B2: the PDF is hosted on drive.google.com (proxy 403) and the old iau.org/static URL returns 404, so it was not opened. NASA SVS 11084 unreachable.
claims.note: 149.598e6 km / c = 499.0 s (8.32 min); perihelion 490.7 s (8.18 min); aphelion 507.4 s (8.46 min); ±1.67% variation, matching SOURCES' ±1.7% and 8.2-8.5 min. 'Eight minutes' is a fair rounding. Measuring from the photosphere rather than the Sun's centre shortens it by ~2.3 s, which does not matter. The 1 AU exact value was checked against the NASA fact sheet (149.598e6 km), not against the IAU text itself.

claims.claim: Getting out was the slow part.
claims.source_checked: https://solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml; NIST c; NSSDC Earth fact sheet
claims.note: This is about 8 minutes against ~1e6 years (MSFC) for the radiative crossing. It brings no new figure.

claims.claim: But it is not the same light.
claims.note: MSFC: in the radiative zone the energy travels as 'radiation (mostly gamma-rays and x-rays)', and the core's energy 'ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'. Light of a different kind leaves the surface, which supports 'not the same light'.

claims.source_checked: https://solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml (read); NASA SVS https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/11084, the source SOURCES cites for absorption/re-emission, was unreachable (curl TLS failure; WebFetch DNS failure; Firecrawl out of credits)
claims.note: This is an absolute claim, and the only source that states the mechanism (SVS: photons absorbed and re-emitted repeatedly) could not be read. MSFC does not say it. Its own wording, 'an individual photon takes about a million years to finally reach the interface layer', could be read by a pedant as the same photon crossing the radiative zone. SOURCES' 'hand-off at 0.7 R' argument ('no photon from the core can be the one that leaves') is the author's inference, not a sentence in MSFC. MSFC says the convection zone is opaque and heat is carried by convection, not that radiation is absent there. To pass: get SVS 11084 (or a textbook with edition stating absorption/re-emission/thermalisation) read and quoted in SOURCES. Or narrow the line to what MSFC supports, e.g. 'The light that leaves is not the light that was made' (gamma/X-rays inside, visible light at the surface).
~1e6 years (MSFC) is fairly called ancient on a human scale. The figure is the same one as in claim 1.

claims.claim: The light is eight minutes old.
claims.source_checked: https://solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml; NIST c; NSSDC Earth fact sheet
claims.note: The age counts from the visible surface. MSFC says the energy leaves the surface as visible light, and the travel time is 8.2-8.5 min (claim 3). This does not depend on claim 6: whatever happens inside, the visible light we see leaves at the photosphere.

claims.claim: Tag '8 MINUTES' / sub 'surface to your skin' + 'not to scale', over Sun and Earth with a pulse crossing the gap
claims.source_checked: NIST c; NSSDC Earth fact sheet
claims.note: Same figure as claim 3, measured from the surface. The shot is labelled not to scale (A6), as it must be, since Earth is drawn far too big and too close.

claims.claim: Tag '100,000+ YEARS' / sub 'energy, core to surface' + 'not one photon · not to scale'
claims.note: MSFC: ~1e6 years from the core to the interface layer, then convection carries heat 'quite rapidly to the surface', so core to surface is more than 1e5 years. 'not one photon' matches the energy framing. The SOURCES fix in claim 1 applies to this tag's sourcing too.

claims.claim: Tag 'THE ENERGY' / sub '100,000+ years getting out'
claims.note: Same as claims 1 and 10, with the same SOURCES fix (claim 1).

claims.claim: Tag 'THE LIGHT' / sub '8 minutes old' + 'not to scale', on the Sun-Earth shot
claims.source_checked: NIST c; NSSDC Earth fact sheet; NASA MSFC interior page
claims.note: Same as claim 8. Labelled not to scale.

claims.claim: Cutaway of the Sun with rings at 0.25 R (core edge) and 0.7 R (base of convection zone)
claims.note: MSFC: core is 'the innermost 25%', radiative zone 'from 25% ... to 70%', convection zone 'the outermost 30%'. SOURCES' extra 0.713 R (Christensen-Dalsgaard, Gough & Thompson 1991) was not verified: Crossref confirms title/journal/volume/page but has no abstract, and ADS was unreachable. It is not needed for a 0.7 ring.

claims.claim: Random-walk path from the centre to the 0.7 ring (radiative transport), then convection above
claims.note: MSFC: energy generated in the core is carried by photons that bounce 'from particle to particle through the radiative zone' to the interface layer, and by convection above it. The animation is labelled not to scale and 'not one photon'.

claims.claim: Path colour by log temperature from 15 MK (r=0), 7 MK (0.25 R), 2 MK (0.7 R), 5,700 K (surface): ~10% of the way to yellow at 0.25 R, ~26% at 0.7 R
claims.note: MSFC: centre about 15,000,000 °C, radiative zone 7,000,000 °C falling to about 2,000,000 °C, visible surface 5,700 K (NSSDC: central 1.571e7 K, effective 5772 K). At MK scale °C vs K does not matter. MSFC also says the core edge is 'half its central value' (7.5 MK). Using that would give 8.8% instead of 9.7%, still about 10%. Recomputed: (log 15e6 - log 7e6)/(log 15e6 - log 5700) = 9.7%; for 2e6 = 25.6%. Violet for MSFC's gamma/X-ray radiation and yellow for visible light at the surface is consistent with the source. The hue is schematic, as SOURCES says.

claims.claim: Rotating convection cells fill the shell between 0.7 R and the surface
claims.note: MSFC: convection zone extends from ~200,000 km depth 'right up to the visible surface', and 'convective motions carry heat quite rapidly to the surface'.

claims.claim: A fan of five short yellow light rays leaves the surface
claims.note: MSFC: the energy 'ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'. Yellow is the conventional, schematic colour for sunlight, not a claim about its spectrum.
